written.myAnswer: The modern periodic table is arranged in increasing atomic number because the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
“Periodic” means that the properties of elements repeat at regular intervals when they are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
Elements in the same group have similar outer-shell electronic configurations and therefore the same number of electrons in their outermost shells.
Place the element according to its atomic number. Its electronic configuration can then help identify its period and group.
The element’s electronic configuration can help determine its period and group. Atomic mass is not the basis for locating elements in the modern periodic table; atomic number is.

The periodic table arranges elements in increasing atomic number and places elements with similar properties in the same groups. It reveals the periodic repetition of properties, making elements easier to study and compare and helping predict their properties.
